trial_name.text: Study WA18062 (Study V), in RA patients with inadequate response to anti-TNF agents

citations.quote: The primary efficacy objective of studies WA17822, WA17823 and WA18062 was to assess the efficacy of TCZ vs. placebo in patients with moderate to severe active RA with regard to reduction in signs and symptoms over 6 months of treatment in combination with background MTX therapy. Studies WA17822 and WA17823 were conducted in patients with an inadequate clinical response to MTX and study WA18062 was conducted in patients who had had inadequate response to one or more anti-TNF therapies.
This statistical review is based on data submitted in studies WA17822, WA17823, WA17824, WA18062, and WA18063.
In all of the pivotal Phase III studies, escape patients could also receive intra-articular corticosteroids or an increase in oral corticosteroid dosage (maximum dose of 10 mg total dose/day).

population.text: Patients >18 years with moderate to severe active RA (ACR criteria; at least 8 tender and 6 swollen joints) with inadequate response to one or more anti-TNF agents

citations.quote: Moderate to severe active RA in patients with inadequate response to anti-TNF agent(s)

In all five studies, patients who were > 18 years of age with active rheumatoid arthritis diagnosed according to the American College of Rheumatology criteria, and had at least 8 tender and 6 swollen joints at baseline were included in the study. The objectives of the studies were similar.

endpoint.text: Proportion of patients achieving an ACR20 response at Week 24

citations.quote: With the exception of WA17823, all studies had a 24-week treatment period and the primary endpoint was the proportion of ACR20 responders at week 24.

n.text: 499 patients randomized (ITT ACR20 analysis: placebo N=158, TCZ 4 mg/kg N=161, TCZ 8 mg/kg N=170)

citations.quote: Total Randomized Patients	623	1196	673	499	1220	537**	1902**

result.text: ACR20 at Week 24: 10% placebo (16/158), 30% TCZ 4 mg/kg (49/161), 50% TCZ 8 mg/kg (85/170); p<0.0001 for both TCZ doses vs placebo

indication.text: Treatment of adult patients with moderately-to severely-active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response to one or more TNF antagonist therapies

citations.quote: ACTEMRA® (tocilizumab) is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with moderately-to severely-active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response to one or more TNF antagonist therapies.

detail.text: WARNING: RISK OF SERIOUS INFECTIONS — patients treated with ACTEMRA are at increased risk for developing serious infections that may lead to hospitalization or death, including TB, bacterial, invasive fungal, viral, and other opportunistic infections; interrupt ACTEMRA if a serious infection develops; perform test for latent TB prior to starting

citations.quote: ## WARNING: RISK OF SERIOUS INFECTIONS

Patients treated with ACTEMRA are at increased risk for developing serious infections that may lead to hospitalization or death [see *Warnings and Precautions* (5.1), *Adverse Reactions* (6.1)]. Most patients who developed these infections were taking concomitant immunosuppressants such as methotrexate or corticosteroids.
- Perform test for latent TB; if positive, start treatment for TB prior to starting ACTEMRA. (5.1)

Certain questions regarding the Financial Disclosure section of the application would require clarification prior to approval.6. Inspection of the Chugai Pharma Manufacturing Company facility in Japan documented numerous deficiencies requiring resolution before approval of the application would be possible.7. citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for the use of Actemra (tocilizumab) for the treatment of active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis in patients 2 years of age and older and a proposed modification to the approved REMS.

description.text: Added labeling on improvement in general health status assessed by the Short Form Health Survey (SF-36)

citations.quote: These Prior Approval supplemental biologics applications provide the inclusion of language regarding the improvement in general health status, assessed by the Short Form Health Survey (SF-36).

description.text: Added new indication for treatment of CAR T cell-induced severe or life-threatening cytokine release syndrome in adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older

citations.quote: The review team recommends regular approval of tocilizumab under 21 CFR 601 for the indication “for the treatment of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell-induced severe or life-threatening cytokine release syndrome in adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older.” The recommended tocilizumab dose is 8 mg/kg for patients \ge 30 kg and 12 mg/kg for patients < 30 kg for up to 4 doses at least 8 hours apart with or without corticosteroids.

description.text: Added new indication for treatment of hospitalized adult COVID-19 patients receiving systemic corticosteroids and requiring supplemental oxygen or ventilation

description.text: Expanded COVID-19 indication to include hospitalized pediatric patients aged 2 years and older receiving systemic corticosteroids and requiring respiratory support
